inputs.text: Israel’s parliament has begun debating a bill that would make execution the default punishment for West Bank Palestinians convicted of murdering Israelis. That is a sweeping use of state power against a specifically targeted population, dressed up as security policy. Itamar Ben-Gvir’s far-right party introduced the legislation, and its passage would be a political victory for him. As opponents warn, the measure is racist and draconian—and there is little reason to believe executions would deter attacks. A policy built on unequal treatment won’t deliver justice or safety.
